clue.text: Fail company, heartless menace right to be arrested by a policeman

indicators.note: with its heart gone, the word menace keeps only its first and last letters
the letter for right is held inside the word for policeman, as a prisoner is held

parts.note: a copper is British slang for a police officer

explanation.surface: A firm fails as a ruthless thug is lawfully taken into custody by an officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' strips the inside of menace, keeping only its ends; 'to be arrested by' holds the right letter in the officer. 'a' is part of the wordplay, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for coming to grief or suffering a heavy fall, so failing badly.

clue.text: Medical practitioner working, in essence, on radius

indicators.note: the word for working goes inside the word for essence

parts.note: the core of something is its essence
on means working or functioning, as a machine is on
R is the abbreviation for radius in geometry

explanation.surface: A doctor is busy, in essence, with a bone of the forearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radius' suggests the forearm bone, but it is only the geometry abbreviation R.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who investigates sudden deaths is often a doctor, hence a medical practitioner.

clue.text: Surreptitiously conveyed money revealed, after heroin's seized

indicators.note: the word for revealed grabs and holds the letter for heroin

parts.note: outed means exposed or revealed publicly
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Cash was passed on in secret and came to light once a drug haul was taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' here places the M before the rest, which follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To form words silently with the lips is to convey them without sound, a secretive way of communicating.

clue.text: Adult tolerated temperature surrounded by odd collection of plants

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: the words for tolerated and temperature sit inside the word for odd

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or strange
bore means endured or tolerated

explanation.surface: A grown-up put up with the heat amid a strange array of greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical garden devoted to trees is a curated collection of growing specimens.

clue.text: Express rebuke? I would

parts.note: a rap is a sharp reprimand or rebuke
I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: A question about whether to voice a reprimand, answered with a willing yes.
explanation.definitionFit: An express train or service is a fast one, so the adjective is a synonym.

clue.text: Standard sticks erected for plant

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something upright means reading the word from the bottom up

parts.note: pins are things that stick or fasten

explanation.surface: A regulation set of canes is put up to support a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A root vegetable grown in gardens is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Variable smell in Scottish river going north brought up

indicators.note: the variable and the smell go inside the turned river
in a down clue, travelling north means the river's name reads upward

parts.note: the Dee flows through Aberdeenshire in Scotland
X is the classic algebraic variable
hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: An unpredictable stink drifting up a Scottish river was raised as an issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going north' turns DEE into EED, which then holds X and HUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A body dug out of the ground is literally raised to the surface.

clue.text: Obliged secretary to look up price for corrupting a rightwinger

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters for secretary are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant or secretary

indicators.note: corrupting a word spoils its order, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative, a political rightwinger

explanation.surface: An assistant, feeling obliged, checks a price to bribe a right-wing politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to look up' makes AP; 'corrupting' turns PRICE into PRECI; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling obliged means feeling grateful, and the answer means expressing gratitude.

clue.text: Dry salesman backtracking causes worry

indicators.note: going back over a path means the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A dull salesman going back on his word makes people anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backtracking' turns BRUTREP as a whole; 'causes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle or trouble someone is to make them anxious, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Penny, bent over and gasping

parts.note: arched means curved or bent over

explanation.surface: A woman named Penny doubles over, struggling for breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' reads as a woman's name but is just the coin abbreviation P.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasping for a drink means desperately thirsty, which is what dried out means.

clue.text: Decisively cutting off a pedantic git in flow

indicators.note: letters in flow are fluid and moving, so they rearrange into a new order

explanation.surface: Firmly interrupting a fussy fool in mid-speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing a head is the most decisive cutting off, and figuratively means depriving a body of its leaders.

clue.text: Cowboy dear to Frenchwoman goes after drove

indicators.note: the French word for dear is placed after the word for drove

parts.note: ran means drove, as in ran someone home
cher is French for dear

explanation.surface: A cowboy, sweet on a French lady, chases after a herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drove' looks like a herd of cattle, fitting the cowboy, but is the past tense of drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs a cattle farm in the American West is popularly a cowboy.

clue.text: Lively game, Andy Murray primarily in charge

indicators.note: being game means willing, so these letters are willing to be rearranged
primarily picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An energetic match, with tennis player Andy Murray mainly in control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' sits naturally with the tennis star but signals that the name before Murray is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of energy and drive, a near synonym of lively.

clue.text: Was anxious about punching bounder

indicators.note: the word for about breaks into the word for bounder, as a fist goes in

parts.note: a cad or bounder is an old British term for a dishonourable man
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone was nervous about hitting a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Having cared about something can mean having worried over it.

clue.text: False bottom in cuddly toy ahead

indicators.note: the word for bottom goes inside the word for cuddly toy

parts.note: a ted is short for a teddy bear
the rump is the bottom or backside
up means ahead, as in a goal up

explanation.surface: A fake rear in a soft toy at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge invented to frame someone is fabricated, therefore false.

clue.text: Experienced, one over the Channel on lake

parts.note: un is French for one, France lying across the English Channel
Derwentwater is a lake in the English Lake District, often called Derwent

explanation.surface: Someone across the Channel, seasoned, sits by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link placing the first piece on top of the second in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through something is to experience or suffer it.

clue.text: Noted a cold, arranged medical

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone noticed a chill and booked a health check.
explanation.definitionFit: Being noted can mean being celebrated, and acclaim is public praise.

clue.text: Departed under army officer's order

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for departed is placed below the officer

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer
the late are the departed, those who have died

explanation.surface: A dead soldier lies beneath a colonel's command.
explanation.definitionFit: To put pages or data into sequence is to collate them, a synonym of arrange in order.

clue.text: Con proceeds, following a head of tourism

indicators.note: the word for proceeds comes after the A

parts.note: gains are proceeds or profits

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A swindle's takings follow a tourist board chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' looks like a swindle, matching the surface, but means the opposing side, as in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: The con side of an argument is the case opposed, so this preposition fits.

clue.text: Advance after crossing India

indicators.note: the word for after spans across the letter for India, holding it

parts.note: post means after, as in post-war
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Pushing forward once a journey across India is done.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward a theory or idea is to propose it, the verb sense of advance.

clue.text: Sack attendant, feeling bad inside

indicators.note: the word for feeling bad sits inside the word for attendant

parts.note: a page is a young attendant
ill means unwell, feeling bad

explanation.surface: Fire the servant, sick at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like dismissal of the attendant, but it is the plundering sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, which is exactly looting.

clue.text: Irons bizarrely hot in three seconds

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the three seconds

parts.note: three words for a second: S, MO (a moment) and S again

indicators.note: bizarrely means oddly, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Pressing gear oddly heats up in just a few seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, short for a moment, is a crossword stand-in for a second alongside S; 'bizarrely' rearranges the word for hot, placed after MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing presses out creases, making cloth flat, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: One politician leaving impersonal, sprawling French city

indicators.note: sprawling means spread out untidily, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the letters for one and the politician depart from the word impersonal

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician quits a cold, sprawling French metropolis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes IMP from IMPERSONAL, leaving ERSONAL; 'sprawling' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A city on the Loire, famed for Joan of Arc, the Maid of its name.

clue.text: Beginning to smile for good child

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A first grin wins a well-behaved youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprog is British slang for a baby or small child.

clue.text: Ban hooligan swallowing ecstasy after sport

indicators.note: the hooligan with ecstasy comes after the sport

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a sport

indicators.note: the word for hooligan takes in the letter for ecstasy

parts.note: a lout is a hooligan
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Bar the thug who took a pill after the rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude a possibility or prohibit something is to bar it, a sense of ban.

clue.text: Longer period of time with northern ruler

parts.note: a year is a period of time
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen as ruler

explanation.surface: A greater stretch of time under a northern monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Longer' reads as a comparative but is one who longs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who yearns is one who longs, a playful agent-noun reading.

clue.text: Protein drink's repellent small container

indicators.note: repellent means revolting, and revolting letters overturn their order

parts.note: ales are drinks, the possessive read as a plural
a tin is a small metal container

explanation.surface: A protein shake's off-putting little canister.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretchy structural protein in skin and connective tissue.

clue.text: Conventions to understand, greet host when partying

parts.note: to get something is to understand it

indicators.note: partying letters get into a wild jumble, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gatherings where one must grasp how to welcome a host at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Conventions are formal meetings or gatherings, and these are informal ones.
